text:
The court will require a greater foundation to establish the records' reliability before admitting them. The defendant's bare statement that he kept the records "on a regular business basis" does not satisfy FRE 803(6) or authenticate computer output under FRE 901(b)(9), so the objections stand until someone explains how the records were made and why the system produces accurate results. Revising my earlier answer: the defendant's availability as a witness does not cure hearsay, since FRE 803 exceptions don't require unavailability and the party-opponent rule doesn't apply to a defendant offering his own statements.

CONFIDENCE: 55
